title: New Unpatched Windows 0-Day FastUnlock Lets Someone Holding a Locked PC Run Programs on It

content.summary: A newly disclosed unpatched zero-day technique called FastUnlock lets someone with physical access to a locked Windows computer start programs without signing in. Whoever uses it gets only a limited account, not administrator control of the machine. The method was posted yesterday by a researcher who uses the handles MSNightmare and Nightmare Eclipse, and the endpoint-security firm ThreatLocker...
content.impact: The implications of this cybersecurity update are significant for digital infrastructure in Tier-1 nations. Experts suggest that such developments could influence both consumer behavior and enterprise-level security protocols in the US, UK, CA, and AU markets.

keyPoints: A new Windows zero-day technique called FastUnlock was disclosed. It allows someone with physical access to a locked Windows computer to run programs without signing in. The method provides a limited account, not administrator control.
